components.detail: Checked on 25 Oct 2026: 70 C flow while charging the cylinder, system pressure 1.9 bar. Manual pressure values: the correct cold filling pressure is 1.0 to 2.0 bar, so this house sits near the top of the range; below 0.8 bar the pressure reading flashes as a warning; below 0.5 bar the boiler switches off and shows F.22; at 2.8 bar and above it shows S.41.

drive.label: House systems quick reference, from the manuals (Drive)

components.how: The boiler heats water in a sealed circuit and sends it where the controller asks: to the radiators, to the underfloor loops, or through a coil inside the Megaflo cylinder to heat the stored tap water. On its display, a tap symbol means it is heating the water tank; a radiator symbol means it is heating the house.
label: Boiler
Vaillant 637
components.name: Boiler
components.what: A Vaillant ecoTEC plus 637 system boiler. It burns gas and makes hot water for the heating system. It is the single heat source for the whole house.

components.detail: Seen on 25 Oct 2026: room 20.5 C, outside 9.5 C. The morning check found the clock showing 5:46 at 8:03 real time, and the date set to 28 Jan 2010. Both were corrected the same morning (the date set to 25 Oct 2026), the controller was put back on Auto, and all of it was confirmed done at 08:43.

drive.label: House systems quick reference, from the manuals (Drive)

components.how: It runs heating and hot water to daily timetables stored in its own clock, so the clock and the calendar date both have to be right: Auto follows the date as well as the time. Hot water modes: Auto follows the timetable, Day keeps the tank hot all the time. Cylinder boost heats the tank once, right away, outside the timetable, then cancels itself. It runs two heating circuits, renamed by Zonito on 25 Oct 2026 to RADIATORS (Day 21.0 C, set-back 18.0 C; was HEATING 1) and UNDERFLOOR (Day 22.0 C, set-back 19.0 C; was HEATING 2), and confirmed set and saved at the controller. Later that morning he tuned it further: the RADIATORS day temperature came down from 24.0 C to 21.0 C (set-back unchanged at 18.0 C) and the hot water generation was split from one long stretch into 05:00 to 10:00 and 17:00 to 22:30; he set Monday first, then copied the same pattern to Tuesday to Sunday himself and confirmed all seven days set. The names rest on the analysis that HEATING 1 serves the radiators and HEATING 2 the ground floor underfloor heating; the installer-screen confirmation of that mapping is now optional. Programmes: hot water generation runs 05:00 to 10:00 and 17:00 to 22:30 (period 3 unused) on all seven days; one heating circuit's Monday runs 05:00-11:30, 12:30-16:30 and 18:00-23:00, the other 06:00-21:30. Sensor offsets are 0.0 K for room and outside temperature, and daylight saving is on Auto. The installer level still opens with the default code; the only change made there was the circuit rename, and no configuration values were altered; the reset to default option was left at No for both choices. The Days at home and Days away windows are both set to a single day in January 2010, so they are inactive.
label: Controller
VRC 470
components.name: Heating controller

status.label: Clock and date corrected; back on Auto

components.what: A Vaillant VRC 470 weather compensator. It is the timetable keeper for heating and hot water, and it adjusts boiler temperature to the weather outside.

components.detail: On the morning of 25 Oct 2026 three baths drained the tank and the timetable had not fired because of the controller clock and date fault. Setting hot water to Day started the reheat, and the immersion heater was switched on at about 08:11 to help, then switched back off once the tank was hot again. Hot water was put back to Auto the same morning. Photos of the cupboard on 25 Oct 2026 show two immersion covers on the tank, and a small dark-screen digital unit on the cupboard wall beside the immersion switch, not yet identified; it may be a timer.

drive.label: Hot water: how it works and the 25 Oct 2026 fix (Drive)
Megaflo Eco installation and servicing manual (Drive)

components.how: Taps draw stored hot water from the tank. The boiler reheats the tank through a coil inside it, only when the controller timetable or a boost asks. Back to back baths can drain the tank; a full reheat takes about 30 to 45 minutes. The hot water target temperature was found set to only 45 C and was raised to 60 C the same morning: 60 C is the legionella-safe storage temperature, and it also makes the 210 litres go further in baths. The tank also has electric immersion backup: two immersion covers are fitted on its side, one upper and one lower, though which element the wall switch controls is unconfirmed. The immersion was off since 10 Oct 2026, switched on for the 25 Oct 2026 reheat and back off the same morning. Standing heat loss is 1.61 kWh per day (the manual table's figure for the nearest listed size).

components.what: A Heatrae Sadia Megaflo Eco unvented cylinder holding 210 litres of hot water. This tank, not the boiler, is what feeds the taps and baths.

components.detail: This circuit is separate from the underfloor wiring centre, so it kept working during the underfloor power fault.
components.how: When the controller calls for heat, the boiler sends hot water around this circuit. The chrome towel rail is heated by boiler water, not electricity; its heat is set by the valves at its base.

top bedroom

components.detail: Found on again on 25 Oct 2026: thermostat on in manual mode, setpoint 20.0 C, floor temperature 25.1 C, not calling for heat at that moment. Same floor that was found running in manual mode on 10 Oct 2026 and switched fully off then.
components.how: A heating mat under the floor warms the tiles directly. On 10 Oct 2026 it was found switched on in manual mode, set to 23 C with the floor near 29 C, even though it was thought to be off since May; it was switched fully off the same day. On 25 Oct 2026 it was found on again in manual mode, this time set to 20.0 C with the floor at 25.1 C, so it was warm but not drawing heat at that moment.

The icons suggest it runs a timed programme rather than a plain manual hold. The slow clock is the only minor point open: its warm periods will land late until the clock is corrected.

It runs a timed programme, warming the floor at set times of day rather than holding one temperature all the time. Zonito calls this the first floor first bathroom.

components.detail: Fault state on 24 Oct 2026: POWER light dark, every zone light dark, the Drayton LP711 timer beside it also blank, while every consumer unit breaker was on. Fix is an electrician visit.

drive.label: Underfloor heating fault: findings and costs (Drive)

components.how: When a thermostat calls for heat, this box powers open that zone's actuator valve, starts the manifold pump and asks the boiler for heat. Its valves are normally shut, so with no power nothing can flow. Its board fuse is a 5 amp anti-surge 20 mm glass fuse, currently stuck fast in its clips. The Zone 4 pump control switch was found set to NO and was moved to YES on 24 Oct 2026, which is correct for underfloor heating, but the box still has no power.
label: Wiring centre
Polypipe UFH4ZW
components.name: Underfloor wiring centre
components.what: A Polypipe UFH4ZW wiring centre. It is the brain of the ground floor underfloor heating: it listens to the room thermostats and opens the valves on the manifold.

components.detail: Pump green light on, flow gauges near zero on all four loops, 24 Oct 2026.

drive.label: Underfloor heating fault: findings and costs (Drive)

components.how: The pump pushes warm water around the loops under the floor. The mixing valve blends the water down to a gentle floor temperature. Each loop has a flow gauge and a valve motor (actuator) opened by the wiring centre. Loop 2 has a plain manual cap instead of a motor, so it has no automatic control. With the wiring centre dead, the pump runs but the valves stay shut and all four gauges read near zero.

pump + 4 loops
components.name: Underfloor manifold and pump
components.what: The pipe hub for the floor heating: two brass bars, four floor loops, a Grundfos UPS2 25-40/60 pump, a thermostatic mixing valve and four flow gauges.

components.detail: The lobby target was raised to 20 C by hand on 24 Oct 2026 while family are staying.
components.how: Each thermostat watches its zone and asks the wiring centre for heat when the room is below target. On 24 Oct 2026 the living hall sat at 18 C against targets above 20 C, calling correctly, but the dead wiring centre could not act on the calls.

lobby, hall x2

status.label: Working, but their calls go nowhere

components.detail: This is the visible symptom of the wiring centre power fault, not a fault in the floor itself.
components.how: Warm water flowing through the loops turns the whole floor into a slow, gentle radiator. A working loop feels warm underfoot. Right now no water can enter the loops because the manifold valves are held shut by the dead wiring centre, so the floor stays cold and the living hall stalls near 20 C.

lobby + living hall

components.detail: Same electrician visit as the wiring centre. The manual is saved in Drive under Household, Manuals.
components.how: It is faulty: it powers up, runs for 3 to 4 minutes, then goes completely dark. The likely cause is a plug, fuse or connection failing as it warms under load, or an overheat cut-out tripping. It uses almost no electricity in this state (about 0.2 kWh per short run), so it is not a bill problem. It is left switched off at the wall; restarting it repeatedly is not safe.

components.how: Tariffs shown on the display: electricity 26.613p per kWh plus 51.83p per day; gas 7.91p per kWh plus 29.33p per day. From 1 to 24 Oct 2026 the house used 367 kWh of electricity (about 15.3 kWh a day) and 467 kWh of gas (about 19.5 kWh a day). Every cost screen on the display reconciles exactly with these tariffs.

scenarios.caption: Floor: warm · Tank: hot · Radiators: on · Car: charging
explanation: A normal day. The boiler heats the house and keeps the tank hot on the controller timetable.
Warm water runs through the floor loops and the radiators. The car charges when it is plugged in, which is the main reason some days use more electricity.

Even on a normal day, one thing stays as it is until fixed: the Dimplex is faulty and off. All three bathroom floors were checked on 25 Oct 2026: the top floor and the en-suite sit in manual mode at 20.0 C, and the family bathroom runs a timed programme, so none of them is a heavy load.
scenarios.name: Normal day

scenarios.caption: Tank: drained, then reheating · Boiler: busy with the tank · Floor: warm
explanation: Three baths back to back drain the 210 litre tank, because taps use stored water, not instant heat from the boiler. This is normal, not a breakdown.
Cylinder boost then points the boiler at the tank alone until it is hot again: about 30 to 45 minutes for a full reheat. House heating pauses while the tank charges.
The immersion heater could reheat the tank with electricity instead, but it stays off to save money.
scenarios.name: Morning baths

scenarios.caption: Floor: cold · Tank: hot · Radiators: on · Controller clock: fixed
explanation: Today, 25 October 2026: the underfloor wiring centre has no power, so its valves stay shut, no water enters the floor loops, and the living hall stalls near 20 C with a cold floor.
The boiler, radiators and hot water run on a separate path and are unaffected. The manifold pump still runs, but it only stirs water inside the manifold.

Separately, the controller clock was found about 2 hours 16 minutes slow with its date set to January 2010, which is why the hot water timetable fired late this morning and the tank ran cold after the baths. The clock and date have since been corrected and Auto restored.
